best_for: People who live in Google's services, and organisations that need one policy across every browser.

points.title: Sign-in is optional
points.text: Google's help says signing in is optional. Without it you browse normally; with it, bookmarks, passwords and other data sync across your devices.

points.title: Windows requirements
points.text: Intel and AMD PCs need Windows 10 or later and a processor with SSE3 (a Pentium 4 class chip or newer). Windows on Arm needs Windows 11.

points.title: macOS floor
points.text: Chrome needs macOS 13 Ventura or newer.

points.title: Official Linux packages
points.text: Google supports 64-bit Ubuntu 18.04+, Debian 10+, openSUSE 15.5+ and Fedora 39+, delivered as .deb and .rpm packages that update through your package manager.

points.title: The Flatpak is not Google's
points.text: The Chrome listing on Flathub is marked unverified, and its page says it is community-provided and not supported by or affiliated with Google. For a supported Linux install use the .deb or .rpm.

points.title: Few old versions to pick from
points.text: Chrome updates itself, and the winget listing keeps very few past releases, so a rollback page here has little to offer for Windows and nothing for Mac or Linux.

points.title: Managed Chrome exists
points.text: Google runs a separate help centre for organisations that manage Chrome through cloud or on-premises policy. We did not confirm its licensing terms.
